optional relative pronoun

The first "that" neither has a preceding antecedent nor a trailing relative clause, so it is not a relative pronoun. Rather, it is a conjunction, or in less traditional language complementizer, for it is introducing the subordinate clause "that pepe is rare as fuck" as an object of the verb "to tell", used here in its transitive sense of "to discern, infer". As such, its role is entirely analogous to, e.g., that of the German "dass" in introducing so-called content clauses.

Regardless, you are however correct that that "that" that that "that" that is demonstrative of "pepe" follows (more clearly, that that "that" that precedes that "that" that precedes "pepe": conjunction–determiner–noun–relative pronoun–determiner–noun–relative pronoun) is optional, although its retainment seems to me recommended since—being as they are already primed by the earlier occurrence of "tell" to expect the imminent approach of some complement that will finally inform them what, exactly, it is that you "could tell by the cached thumbnail"—the reader is otherwise wont to initially misparse the lone remaining demonstrative "that" as instead being the conjunctive "that" of a that-clause.
